claims: First-order particle-vibration coupling H' = - sum_mu alpha_lambda_mu k_lambda(r) Y_lambda_mu* describes the scattering of nucleons via phonon emission and absorption, with surface form factor k_lambda(r) = -R_0 dV_0/dr.

Coupling to high-lying giant resonances (e.g. 2 hbar omega_0 ISGQR) polarizes the closed-shell core, inducing effective polarizability chi_F = kappa alpha_0^2 / (hbar omega - Delta E) and establishing microscopic effective charges e_eff(p) ~ 1.5e and e_eff(n) ~ 0.5e.

Exchange of virtual collective phonons between valence nucleons generates long-range effective two-body interactions, providing the microscopic origin of the quadrupole-quadrupole (Q.Q) and pairing forces.

The self-consistent RPA dispersion relation 1/kappa = sum_{ph} |<p|F|h>|^2 [1/(epsilon_p - epsilon_h - hbar omega) + 1/(epsilon_p - epsilon_h + hbar omega)] accounts for ground-state quantum fluctuations (backward-going Y amplitudes), explaining both the energy depression of collective phonons and the huge (X+Y)^2 collective transition enhancement.
